tells.1: none, though 'Maybe you gave money, raised funds or just cheered us on. Either way...' is a slightly tidy rhetorical turn
tells.2: Stock scenic opener ('As autumn settles over the hills') plus a polished 'Whether you've donated, raised funds or cheered us on' triad
tells.3: Generic boilerplate ('your generosity helps us be there when we're needed'), and the closing 'you're welcome' reads oddly
tells.4: Cleft emphasis ('your donations are what let us') and a personified vehicle 'joining the team'
tells.6: Em dash and an inflated 'a welcome addition... a reminder of what your support makes possible', plus 'heartfelt thank you'

reason: Version 5 reads most like a real volunteer wrote it: rambling, with '1st November' and 'pretty busy', but it is clunky and thin on the invitation. Version 1 keeps that natural, specific voice ('We can't wait to see it', 'Come and say hello') while being clear and complete, so it is the best one to send.
